turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `composition` (absorber), `architecture` (n-i-p =
regular, p-i-n = inverted), `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode),
`etl` (electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Each row is a device
CONFIGURATION whose efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently
fabricated cells, so it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single
champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_open_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_open_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
## Reasoning from device physics

**What the training set says works (≥19–23 %):**

1. **Triple/double‑cation Pb–I(Br) absorbers** (FAMAPbBrI, CsFAMAPbBrI) — best bulk quality + benign band gap. Pure Sn, Bi, Sb, Ge compositions and wide‑gap CsPbBr are all capped far below (0.1–10 %) by deep defect states and huge V_OC deficits, so every Sn/Bi/Sb/Br‑only candidate (c003, c016, c020, c037, c046, c053, c054, c066, c068, c072, c075, c076, c078, c080, c096…) is eliminated.
2. **n‑i‑p with TiO₂‑c|TiO₂‑mp or SnO₂ + a high‑mobility, well‑aligned HTM + Au.** The very top of the training set is exactly this stack with an *engineered hole contact / passivated perovskite–HTM interface*: `OAI | DM` → 22.91; `CH3O‑PEIA | Spiro` → 22.05; `Trimethylamine oxide` → 21.3; `SrCl₂ | Spiro` → 20.8. The recurring lesson: the perovskite/HTM interface is the dominant recombination channel, and a passivating interlayer or a superior dopant‑free HTM (DM, fluorene‑type) buys 1–3 % absolute.
3. **p‑i‑n with C60|BCP + PTAA (or SAM) + Cu** is the other high branch (18.2–20.3 %); adding a PFN‑Br/polyelectrolyte wetting‑dipole layer on PTAA improves hole extraction and reduces shunt/interface recombination.
4. Penalties: PEDOT:PSS HTL (too shallow work function → V_OC loss, ~13–16 % ceiling), carbon back contacts without HTM, plastic (PET/PEN) substrates, ZnO ETL on MA‑containing films (chemical decomposition), and exotic/insulating novel ETLs.

**Selection:**

- **c019** — FAMAPbBrI / TiO₂‑c|TiO₂‑mp / **DM** / Au. DM is the fluorene‑terminated dopant‑free HTM that gave the single best entry in the training set (22.91 %); its deep HOMO (~‑5.4 eV) and dopant‑free, pin‑hole‑free film give both high V_OC and stability. Strongest expected performer.
- **c085** — CsFAMAPbBrI p‑i‑n, C60|BCP / **PTAA|PFN‑Br** / Cu. Matches the best inverted stack in training (20.1 %) with an added conjugated‑polyelectrolyte dipole layer that improves perovskite wetting on PTAA and hole selectivity.
- **c015** — CsFAMAPbBrI **| (EPA)PbI** 2D capping layer on the mesoporous‑TiO₂/Spiro reference stack. The 2D/3D surface reconstruction is the canonical route to suppressed surface recombination (cf. `FAMAPbBrI | (HTAB)…` 19.95, `OAI | DM` 22.91).
- **c079** — FAMAPbBrI / SnO₂‑np / **CsPbBr₃‑np | Spiro** / Au. SnO₂ gives the lowest‑hysteresis, best‑aligned electron contact; the wide‑gap CsPbBr₃ nanocrystal interlayer acts as an electron‑blocking/passivating buffer at the hole contact.
- **c062** — FAMAPbBrI / **SnO₂‑np | PCBM‑60** / Spiro / MoO₃|Au. The fullerene‑capped SnO₂ passivates oxide surface traps (training analogues: SnO₂‑c|PCBM 14–19 %, TiO₂‑c|PCBM stacks strong), and MoO₃ ensures ohmic hole extraction into Au.

Near misses: c061 (C60‑SAM/SnO₂, CsFAPbI), c099 (Au‑nw|Spiro), c092, c045, c059, c093 — all likely 19–20 % but with slightly less proven interface passivation.

**Final: c019, c085, c015, c079, c062**
